089be68b-0138-4bbc-a629-1f1259ea3a1e.text: Add dark mode to the checkout. The colours live in src/theme; start from the tokens, not from the components.
The checkout uses 31 hard-coded colours outside `src/theme`. I will add dark values for each token first, then replace the hard-coded ones so the components need no changes.
Do not touch the payment provider iframe.
Understood, the iframe keeps its own styling. I added the dark token set and moved 28 of the 31 colours onto tokens. The three left are inside the iframe wrapper, which I left alone.
Check the contrast of every form field and fix what fails AA.
The card number and expiry fields pass. The error text on the CVC field is 3.9:1, below the 4.5:1 limit. I will raise it to the `danger-strong` token and run the screenshot tests.

f3a379f4-1054-4974-ae7f-1b1651fc9aaa.text: Invoice export runs inside the request and times out for big accounts. Move it to the job queue, keep the same CSV format.
The export builds the whole file in memory inside the request. I will split it: the endpoint creates a job, a worker writes the CSV in chunks and stores it.
Keep the endpoint, it should answer 202 with a job id.
Done. `POST /exports` now answers `202` with `{job_id}`, and `GET /exports/:id` returns the status and the file link when it is ready.
Add a retry when the database times out, with a cap.
The worker now retries a timed-out export up to five times with a growing delay. I am writing the test that makes the database slow on purpose.

f99547eb-fa3f-49b4-a326-3b55de7c0207.text: Upgrade date-fns to version 4 and fix whatever breaks.
I checked the usage first: `format` and `parseISO` appear in 14 files and keep working. Two files use `zonedTimeToUtc`, which version 4 renames. Those need a small change after the install.
Keep the version pinned, no caret.
I am ready to install date-fns 4.1.0, pinned. It needs your OK to run the install command.

073b2574-302c-44c1-aaa3-92e6901564b5.text: Webhook deliveries hammer customers that are slow or down. Propose a retry policy with backoff and show me the options.

Today a failed delivery is retried three times in a row with no delay. I read the delivery code and last month’s logs: 60% of the retries hit an endpoint that is still down. I will draft two schedules with exponential backoff.
Simulate each option against last month’s failures.
Simulated on 41,000 failed deliveries. Option A: 5 attempts over 1 hour. Option B: 8 attempts over 24 hours. Both cut the retry load on a down endpoint by more than 90%.
Add jitter so retries do not line up.

Jitter is in: each delay varies by up to 20%. Both options keep the retry load under 2% of normal traffic. Five attempts over one hour gives up sooner; eight over 24 hours rescues 11% more deliveries but keeps failed events around longer. Which one do you want?

4cb1c619-ef09-4107-a61a-86d0badf0db2.text: Rename the staging queue to match the new naming rules and show me the plan.
The name is changed in the module. `terraform plan` shows 1 to destroy and 1 to add: the queue is replaced, not renamed.
Is anything still in the queue?
Terraform cannot rename a queue in place: it will delete it and create a new one. There are 42 messages in it right now. I can keep the old name instead, or you can drain it first.

0da229d8-6338-4b47-a3dd-919e3657cd51.text: The login test fails about one run in ten on CI. Find out why and fix it.
I ran it 30 times locally with the CPU throttled and it failed 4 times, always on the same line: the test clicks "Sign in" while the form is still loading its fields.
Run it 50 times to be sure.
The test now waits for the form to be ready before it clicks. Fifty runs in a row passed, throttled and not. PR 217 is ready to merge.
